newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, October 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, October 7.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

*Prime minister Romano Prodi rejects former president Francesco Cossiga's proposal to call a referendum over constitutional reforms and reaffirms such reforms must be carried out by the all-party bicameral commission (all).
*Cesare Salvi, leader of Upper House deputies of the Democratic party of the left (PDS), says some investigating techniques used by Milan magistrates proved dangerous (all).
*The Pope entered Rome's Gemelli hospital where he is due to undergo an operation to remove his appendix, amid speculation that he might be suffering from something more serious (all).
* The government is seeking alternative proposals to the new house tax included in the 1997 budget (Sole 24 Ore).
* The second tranche sale of state energy giant Eni gets underway today with the Treasury announcing the amount of shares to be floated (Sole 24 Ore).

* Franco Tato', chief executive of electricity utility Enel, questions the state's role in privatizations. "As long as the state holds on to a golden share there can't be real separation...privatization means the state selling 51 pct of a company's shares". The sell off of Enel is due to take place in 1997 after the privatization of Stet (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
